w:r.w:t: This Product Requirements Document (PRD) defines the end-to-end functional, operational, and technical requirements for the Reception & Patient Access Module of the Hospital Management System (HMS). The module serves as the primary digital nerve-centre for all patient-facing workflows at the front desk of a multispeciality hospital — covering appointment booking, patient registration, admission, discharge, billing, refund processing, emergency triage handoff, pharmacy coordination, lab requisitioning, and post-visit customer support.

Large multispeciality hospital chains such as Apollo Hospitals, Max Healthcare, Yatharth Hospital, Medanta, and Fortis operate at immense throughput — thousands of OPD visits, hundreds of admissions, and dozens of surgical procedures daily. Their competitive advantage rests heavily on a frictionless patient experience from the first point of contact (the reception desk) to discharge and beyond.
The Reception Module must therefore function not merely as an appointment scheduler, but as a unified patient access platform that:
Eliminates physical paperwork and manual handoffs between departments
Enables real-time visibility of bed availability, doctor schedules, OT slots, and diagnostic queues
Ensures regulatory compliance — ABDM/Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, NABH, MCI standards
Delivers measurable NPS improvement through reduced wait times and proactive communication
Generates revenue-cycle-friendly billing data from the first patient touchpoint

Every patient interaction — from the moment a query is raised to the day a bill is settled — is handled through a single intelligent reception platform that is fast, accurate, empathetic, and audit-ready.
Daily workflow execution, data entry, patient queries
The following functional areas are fully within scope of this PRD:
Patient Registration & Master Data Management (UHID creation, KYC)
Appointment Management — OPD, specialist, telemedicine, walk-in
2.2 Out of Scope (Handled by Other Modules)

Handles 120–200 patient interactions per day across OPD, admission, and discharge. Highly fluent with computers. Pain points: switching between 5 different legacy screens, manual bed-availability calls to wards, frequent billing discrepancies. Needs a unified single-screen dashboard.

Works in the 24×7 emergency reception bay. Must triage incoming patients within 60 seconds, activate trauma codes, coordinate ambulance tracking, and immediately notify treating specialists. Works under extreme time pressure with zero tolerance for system lag.

First-time visitor from a tier-2 city. Limited tech literacy. Speaks Hindi. Needs guided kiosk flow with vernacular language support, printed token slips, and WhatsApp-based status updates. Extremely sensitive to wait times and billing transparency.

Verifies cashless eligibility, submits pre-auth requests, and tracks claim status across 15–20 patients per day. Needs direct insurance portal integration and document upload capability from the HMS reception screen.

Monitors daily OPD load, admission rate, average wait time, and revenue by speciality. Needs real-time executive dashboard with drill-down capability. Runs monthly KPI reviews. Requires scheduled PDF report emails.
3.2 Core Patient Journey — OPD Visit (Happy Path)
Online portal / WhatsApp / kiosk / call centre
Nurse module → auto-populated in doctor view
Every patient must be issued a Unique Health ID (UHID) upon first registration. The system shall support the following registration modes:
Walk-in registration at reception counter with Aadhaar OTP / manual ID upload
Pre-registration via hospital website or mobile app (with QR code check-in on arrival)
Emergency registration (minimal fields — Name, Age, Gender, Mobile) with full KYC deferred
ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account) ID linking — mandatory for government scheme patients
Male / Female / Other / Prefer not to say

On mobile number or Aadhaar input, the system shall perform real-time fuzzy-match lookup against the UHID database. If a match is found with ≥ 85% confidence, it shall display the existing record for the receptionist to confirm before creating a duplicate. Auto-merge facility shall be available to administrators.
Multiple family members may be linked under a Head-of-Family account to allow shared appointment booking, consolidated billing, and corporate health package assignment.
The appointment subsystem handles OPD scheduling, telemedicine, specialist referrals, and procedure pre-booking across all channels.
Hospital website — real-time slot availability with online payment
Mobile app (iOS + Android) — native booking with push notifications
WhatsApp chatbot — conversational booking using Twilio / WATI integration
IVR / Call Centre — integrated CTI screen-pop with auto UHID lookup
Kiosk — self-service touchscreen at hospital entrance (vernacular language support)
Third-party aggregators — Practo, Google Health, 1mg (via API)
First-time visit to a speciality; full slot duration
Shorter slot (configurable); auto-linked to previous visit
Zoom / Jitsi link auto-generated; accessible in patient app
Procedure room booking + pre-procedure instructions sent
Linking report from external hospital; structured upload
Geo-tagged scheduling; assigned to visiting physician
Doctor availability configured by department head (days, session times, max daily cap)
Buffer slots (10%) held for walk-ins and emergencies — configurable per doctor
Overbooking prevention with real-time lock (optimistic concurrency on slot reservation)
Double-booking alert for doctors with overlapping OPD + OT schedules
Auto-waitlist: if a slot is full, patient is added to queue and notified on cancellation
Recurring appointment series for chronic disease patients (e.g. monthly dialysis)
Doctor leave / on-call override — notify affected patients and offer rebooking
WhatsApp + SMS + email with iCal attachment
Slot released; refund initiated if prepaid
On patient check-in (kiosk / counter), system generates a token (e.g. C-042 for Cardiology)
Estimated waiting time displayed on TV screens at waiting areas (WebSocket-based live update)
Receptionist can manually advance, skip, or hold tokens
Priority queue flags: Senior Citizen (65+), Pregnant, Wheelchair, VIP, Diplomatic
Inter-department token transfer (e.g. OPD → Lab → Pharmacy) with unified queue view
Queue analytics: average wait time by hour, peak load heatmap, doctor utilisation
FR-4 Admission Management (ADT — Admit, Discharge, Transfer)
Doctor issues admission advice note from EMR or receptionist initiates on verbal order
Admission form auto-populated from UHID — patient / guardian e-sign (OTP-based)
Admission type selected: General / Emergency / Day-care / ICU / Surgical / Maternity
Bed allotment from real-time bed matrix (ward, room type, floor, gender-segregation rules)
Estimated length of stay (ELOS) entered — used for bed planning
Advance deposit collected and linked to admission episode
Diet order, nursing assignment, and treating consultant linked
Wristband / RFID tag printed at reception desk
Notification sent to ward nurse, treating doctor, housekeeping for room preparation
A real-time, colour-coded bed matrix shall be available to receptionists and ward coordinators:
Filters: Ward, Floor, Room Type (General / Semi-private / Private / ICU / NICU / PICU), Speciality, Gender. Search by bed number or patient name.
Transfer initiated by treating doctor / charge nurse — approved by receiving ward
Reception notified; bed matrix updated in real-time
Patient wristband reprinted if ward changes
Billing episode continues under same admission ID (no new UHID)
Discharge order raised by treating physician in EMR
Reception receives discharge alert — final bill consolidation triggered
All department charges fetched: pharmacy, lab, OT, nursing, consumables, room
Insurance / TPA deduction applied if applicable — balance payable calculated
Patient / guardian reviews bill on screen (digital) or printed summary
Payment collected (cash / card / UPI / NEFT) or credit note issued
Discharge summary generated as PDF — emailed + WhatsApp
Bed released → housekeeping notified for cleaning
ABHA-linked health records updated via FHIR API
Death certificate issuance workflow — linked to CMO / MO counter-signature
MLC flag on registration — police notification module with auto-generated MLC number
Body handover documentation with next-of-kin verification
Billing freeze and final settlement process with legal heir
The emergency reception workflow is optimised for speed — a patient must be registered, triaged, and handed off to clinical staff within 3 minutes of arrival:
Ambulance pre-notification: Paramedic calls ahead; ETA + chief complaint captured; ER team alerted
Patient arrives — UHID lookup by name+DOB or Aadhaar (≤ 5 seconds)
If unknown — anonymous 'John Doe' / 'Jane Doe' registration with sequential ID
Triage nurse assigns level: ESI-1 (Resuscitation) → ESI-5 (Non-urgent)
Triage level drives queue priority and room/bay assignment
On-call doctor notified via in-app push + overhead PA system integration
Ambulance log entry created (Vehicle No., Paramedic Name, Pickup Location)
All on-call staff paged; OT + ICU on standby
Crash cart team dispatched; clock started
Isolation bay activated; Poison Control consulted
Security + law enforcement; HMS logs frozen
Automatic MLC flag on admission for: RTA, burns, assault, poisoning, drowning
System generates MLC document with sequential number — prints in 1-click
Police station notification log maintained with timestamp and officer name
OPD Bill — consultation fee + investigation charges + pharmacy
IP (Inpatient) Bill — continuous accrual during admission; interim bills on request
Package Bill — fixed price for procedures (e.g. delivery package, joint replacement)
Day-care Bill — OT / procedure charges without overnight stay
Emergency Bill — ER charges + ambulance + initial stabilisation
Charges auto-posted from: Lab (on sample collection), Pharmacy (on dispensing), OT (on start), Radiology (on scan), Nursing (consumable scanning)
Manual charge posting by receptionist for: miscellaneous, attendant cot, TV, phone, guest meals
Package overage alert: if services exceed package cap, incremental billing auto-triggered
GST applicability by service category — configurable tax rules per state
Dynamic QR display; payment status webhook
Hospital wallet; prepaid health card redemption
Bajaj Finserv / CASHe integration for large bills

Digital invoice sent instantly via WhatsApp + email; print available on demand

Bulk invoice for corporate: Excel-exportable claim file with UHID + diagnosis codes
Advance collected at admission — linked to episode ID
Advance balance shown on billing screen throughout stay
Top-up alerts when balance < 20% of estimated total bill
Advance refund initiated on discharge if balance > final bill
Patient cancels pre-paid appointment — refund per cancellation policy (T-24h: 100%; T-2h: 50%; <2h: 0%)
Discharge bill less than advance collected — balance refunded
Lab test / procedure cancelled after charge posting — credit note + refund
Two payments received for same bill — auto-detected; refund raised
Pre-auth refused after admission — renegotiation or patient billing
Partial bill settlement + DAMA refund policy applied
Refund request raised at reception or patient portal
Reason code selected from predefined list (mandatory)
Auto-routing: Cash refund ≤ ₹500 → cashier; ₹501–₹5,000 → billing supervisor; > ₹5,000 → CFO
Approval notification via in-app + email to approver
On approval: payment reversal initiated to original payment mode
Refund confirmation SMS / WhatsApp to patient with reference number

Refund log maintained with approver name, timestamp, reason — fully auditable
TPA master database pre-loaded with 50+ insurers (Star, HDFC Ergo, New India, Medi-assist etc.)
Eligibility check at check-in: API call to TPA portal; response in ≤ 5 seconds
Pre-auth request generated from HMS with ICD-10 diagnosis + estimated cost
Pre-auth tracking: Pending / Approved / Partially Approved / Rejected — status on dashboard
Final claim package: discharge summary + itemised bill + investigation reports — one-click PDF bundle
Co-payment calculation and collection at discharge
Empanelled government schemes: CGHS, ESI, Ayushman Bharat PMJAY — separate claim workflows
Denial management: rejection reason captured; appeal documentation support
Prescription received from doctor EMR — auto-displayed on reception pharmacy queue
Patient directed to hospital pharmacy with token; estimated wait time displayed
Prescription printed as QR-coded slip if patient goes to external pharmacy
Inpatient: medication requests routed from ward to central pharmacy; delivery tracked

Lab test orders placed from reception for standalone diagnostics (non-doctor walk-in)

OT slots visible in real-time: Theatre number, duration, Surgeon, Anaesthetist, Scrub nurse

Day-of-surgery check-in at reception — pre-op hold verified, wristband re-confirmed
In-person: Dedicated help desk counter at reception with escalation SLAs
Phone: Integrated call centre with CTI screen-pop; call recording; UHID auto-link
WhatsApp: Business API — 24×7 bot for common queries; live agent handoff
Email: Support inbox with auto-acknowledgement and ticket ID

Query / complaint raised — categorised: Billing, Clinical, Service, Facility, Waiting Time, Staff
Priority assigned: P1 (Clinical Safety) → P4 (General Feedback)
Assigned to relevant department with SLA clock started
Auto-escalation if SLA breached: P1 > 1h → CMO; P2 > 4h → HOD; P3 > 24h → Manager
Resolution entered; patient notified; satisfaction rating collected

All patient-facing communications shall be managed through a centralised notification engine:
Appointment reminders, bill, reports, discharge summary, CSAT
OTP, fallback for WhatsApp opt-outs, critical alerts
Missed-call booking; appointment reminders for non-smartphone users
Queue token display, estimated wait time, health tips

All messages shall support 10 regional languages: English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Bengali, Marathi, Gujarati, Punjabi. Template management console for marketing team to create / approve WhatsApp templates.
5,000 appointments/day on a single HMS instance
Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): 15 predefined roles; custom role builder for hospitals
